items.headline: Markets (wk of Nov 2): worst week since the April 2025 tariff crash — S&P 500 -2.7% to 7,376.86, Nasdaq -3.4% to 24,579.42 (slid into correction Thursday) on an AI-valuation repricing (capex-payback doubts + post-election uncertainty), partly clawed back by a Friday chip-led bounce; 10-yr Treasury eased ~7bps on the week to 4.86% but rose Friday after a strong Oct jobs report kept a December Fed hike in play

fal (inference infrastructure for image/video/audio models) closed a $1.3B Series F at a $16B valuation (Nov 3), led by Bessemer with Nvidia, Sound Ventures, T. Rowe Price — doubling its $8B April valuation in seven months; CEO Burkay Gur said the round is large because demand outran compute (had to rate-limit customers over the summer); ~$800M annualized revenue

OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber (early Nov), an application-gated reasoning model for offensive/defensive security that broke into 79.4% of simulated enterprise targets in under 9 minutes in internal pentests; access restricted because the capability is dual-use; landed in a dense frontier-release week

Musk said (Nov 6) Tesla will 'probably' RENT Optimus humanoid robots rather than sell them, starting ~$30K and falling toward ~$20K, external deliveries ~end-2027 as rentals, AI5-powered version ~April 2027; claimed Optimus will be 5x more productive than the average human — reframing embodied AI as robots-as-a-service

Anthropic IPO priced and dated (Nov 10): roadshow launched, 825M Class A shares at $70-78 for a $1.3-1.45T valuation, Nasdaq debut Thursday Nov 19 — band came in below the $1.5-2T chatter around the Oct S-1; first hard public read on how to price a frontier lab

Anthropic shipped a workplace suite (Nov 10): Claude Sheets, Meetings and Whiteboards in beta plus Claude Data (formerly Dashboards) GA; Claude Meetings can join a video call as a visible participant and turn discussion into notes/action items/tasks — frontier labs moving up the stack into owned workflows

Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro (Nov 2), an ultra-wide Mixture-of-Experts model, posted verified-coding results beating DeepSeek-V3 — continuing the open-weight cadence that keeps resetting the price-performance floor

a16z kept writing through the selloff (early Nov): co-led a $375M Series C for Northwood Space (ground-station infrastructure, with DFJ Growth) and led a $75M Series B for robotics-labor startup Tutor Intelligence; a16z now >$100B AUM, Speedrun team grew 359% in a year

Trend: AI-capex math becoming the whole debate — 5 hyperscalers on track to spend ~$660-725B on AI data-center capex in 2026 (up from ~$410B in 2025) with growing 'circular financing' concern; Gartner estimate that data centers need ~$8.5T cumulative revenue through 2030 vs ~$3.6T realistic demand, leaving $4T+ exposed to write-down risk

Trend: 'AI employees' getting real system access and real seed checks — Phaze (a16z seed) giving people AND AI agents access to computers; Clark raised an $11M seed for 'autonomous AI employees' for audit work; agents graduating from chat to operating software and taking actions (permissions, payments)

Cycling: 2027 grid reshaping — Netcompany-Ineos enters its first full year backed by Danish AI tech firm Netcompany; active transfer market (Alpecin bulking up Classics/sprint roster with Mihkels/Garcia Cortina/van Uden; Arnaud de Lie expected to leave Lotto-Intermarche)

Learn (video): 'Multi-Agent Workflows in Claude Code: Skills, Subagents & Handoffs (2026)' — build-along on orchestrating a team of agents with handoffs; paired with 'Build Your First AI Agent in 30 Minutes (Zero Code)' (uploaded Nov 9) as an FAU-ready on-ramp

Learn (research): 2026 cognitive-offloading work documents deskilling — clinicians' ability to detect tumors WITHOUT AI dropped ~6% three months after AI assistance was introduced; higher confidence in AI correlates with less critical thinking; FAU 'AI for Business Leaders' material

Markets (wk of Oct 26): AI trade cracked again — S&P 500 -0.6% wk, Nasdaq -2% (QQQ -3.5% Fri, worst day since June) on Intel cash-burn warning + Amazon AI capex reviving 'does the buildout pay back?' doubts; Fed held 3.75-4.0% Oct 28 with 2 dissents FOR a hike + a St. Louis Fed call that rates may need to rise again

Anthropic filed its S-1 (Oct 26) for a November Nasdaq IPO under ticker 'ANT' at a reported $1.5-2T targeted valuation (up from $965B private round in May); prospectus shows $16.3B H1 2026 revenue vs an $80.7B net loss, founders retain 50.1% voting control; among the largest-ever tech IPOs

OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 'Terra' (broadly available this week) — a model built to see a computer screen, operate applications, and finish multi-step workplace tasks faster/cheaper; more than doubled its prior software-engineering benchmark and cut factual errors in internal tests; a push into computer-use agents

Dulo, an AI engineering startup, closed a $130M seed (Oct 30) backed by Eric Schmidt, John Doerr, and DST Global — one of the largest seeds of the year, landing the same day public AI stocks sold off; headlined a $6B+ US venture week (Kalshi, Cohere, defense, advanced manufacturing)

Frontier-model race ran hot: Google introduced Gemini 4 'Carbon' (Oct 28, strongest for cybersecurity + long-running work) and previewed Genie 4 (world model with native audio); DeepSeek V4.1 dropped Oct 29; OpenAI said internal models produced novel mathematical proofs

Anthropic shipped Claude for Legal 'artifacts' (Oct 28) — ready-to-use interactive legal tools teams adapt with their own data/connectors and share across the business; a frontier lab moving up the stack into vertical, workflow-owning products

Tesla will open Optimus reservations in early December (Oct 30) — a customer waitlist for its humanoid robot after starting production-quality builds in Fremont; external business deliveries still targeted late 2027

Cycling: BMC will enter women's professional road racing and expand investment in off-road/gravel athletes (Oct 28) while closing its XC mountain-bike team — a reallocation toward the sport's growth areas; follows the recent Specialized-Quick-Step split reshaping the 2027 grid

Trend: agent governance becoming its own product category — Dataiku shipped Agent Management (GA Oct, discovers every AI agent a company runs regardless of platform + measures business value); Meta (Muse for SMB), Oracle, ServiceNow racing to let non-engineers build agents

Trend: on-device/open models commoditizing the base layer — Opera announced 'WebAI' (Oct 27), a proposed web standard to run open-weight models like Gemma locally in the browser; DeepSeek V4.1 (Oct 29) continued the open-weight cadence resetting the price-performance floor

Learn (research): 'Confidence Without Competence' — Microsoft-CMU study finds knowledge workers who trust generative AI more report doing less critical thinking; developers who delegated coding to AI shipped working code but failed conceptual checks; antidote is making AI disagree with you; FAU teaching material

Markets (wk of Oct 19): risk-off rotation — S&P 500 ~7,624 (-0.5% wk), Nasdaq -0.7% (QQQ ~$703 after a ~2.9% midweek drop) as investors fled AI-spending exposure into staples/energy/utilities; 10-yr Treasury broke below 5% (~4.95% Thu, biggest 1-day drop since Mar 2023) before bouncing to ~5.0%; Fed expected to hold 3.75-4.0% Oct 28

Tenstorrent (Jim Keller) closed a $1.5B Series E at a $6.2B post-money valuation (Oct 19), led by Trace Capital and Innovation X with ARK, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Morgan Stanley, Sandisk, Tether; scales Galaxy AI servers + open RISC-V silicon and open-weight models — the open/licensable alternative to Nvidia

Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet (Oct 21), a standalone proactive-agent app on Claude Opus 5.5: sends a morning brief across connected apps, keeps working in its own cloud VM with a browser, checks in before sensitive actions; answer to OpenAI 'Dots' and Meta 'Muse'; Pro/Max in the US

a16z is renaming its crypto arm 'a16z Frontier' (Oct 22) and broadening its mandate from blockchain into AI, autonomous machines, and networks connecting people and AI agents; AI now ~64% of a16z's activity; topped the 2026 Strebulaev-Jackson AI venture ranking

Flapping Airplanes, a year-old AI research lab, raised a $1B Series A at a $6B valuation (Oct 21) — nine months after a $180M seed — led by Index, Lux, Sequoia, GV, Kleiner Perkins; the week's clearest froth marker as public AI multiples compress
Otter.ai closed a $320M growth round (Oct 20, General Catalyst) for its meeting-transcription + AI-assistant platform — applied-AI productivity now a growth-stage bet, not a feature

Tesla started Optimus production in Fremont (Oct 21) — first production-quality units — but pushed customer deliveries to ~Q2 2027 (hands/durability/AI 'still need work'); Q3 profit fell 43%; unsupervised FSD for customer cars slid to mid-2027

Cycling: 2027 transfer market and UCI reshuffle — Tao Geoghegan Hart to EF Education-EasyPost, Victoire Berteau to Canyon-SRAM; UCI's Oct 15 registration deadline left TotalEnergies, Kern Pharma, Flanders-Baloise, Euskaltel off the provisional 2027 list pending paperwork
Learn (video): 'Vercel's CEO Just Unveiled The Greatest AI Coding Workflow Ever' (Oct 19) — breaks Guillermo Rauch's AI coding workflow into 7 repeatable tips, recreated in Claude Code
Learn (video): 'Build a Social Media AI Agent Team Using Claude Code & Next.js' (Oct 16) — full build-along course on standing up a coordinated team of agents with handoffs; teaching artifact for FAU
